results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?

status_messages.message: Refining tool choice for VFB query

results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is the part of the mushroom body closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. 

This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain (VFB) evidence, specifically from the "focus_region" description and the "PartsOf" query preview rows. 

For more detailed information about the subdivisions of the mushroom body, you can explore the VFB queries and previews, such as the "PartsOf" query, which lists the parts of the mushroom body, including the adult mushroom body dorsal accessory calyx, adult mushroom body lateral calyx, layer of mushroom body slice, pedunculus divide of adult mushroom body, and pedunculus neck of adult mushroom body. 

Additionally, you can use the VFB tool to explore the neurons that are part of the mushroom body, such as the neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, which are listed in the "NeuronsPresynapticHere" query preview rows. 

Please let me know if you would like to explore any of these options further.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The LPLC2 visual neuron type is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. It has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. It projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. The activity of LPLC2 elicits a jump escape response.

LPLC2 is a cholinergic neuron, and there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe. The neuron type is associated with the adult stage and is part of the visual system.

VFB provides evidence for the connectivity of LPLC2, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes. The downstream connectivity classes include adult VPNd1 lineage neurons, lobula plate-lobula columnar neurons LPLC2, adult cholinergic neurons, and adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neurons 111. The upstream connectivity classes include adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, T5b neurons, T4c neurons, and transmedullary neurons Tm5Y.

Genetic tools for labeling LPLC2 include split-GAL4 drivers such as P{R12E04-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R19G02-p65.AD} and P{R75G12-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R19G02-p65.AD}, as well as expression patterns like P{VT007194-GAL4} and P{GMR75G12-GAL4}.

Publications related to LPLC2 include those by Wu et al. (2016), Klapoetke et al. (2017), and Tanaka and Clark (2022), which provide information on the neuron's anatomy, connectivity, and function.

Overall, the LPLC2 visual neuron type plays a crucial role in detecting looming stimuli and eliciting a jump escape response in Drosophila. Its unique anatomy and connectivity make it an important component of the visual system.

results.title: Comparative anatomy
results.question: How does the organisation of the antennal lobe compare between adult and larval Drosophila?
results.response:
The organization of the antennal lobe in adult and larval Drosophila differs in terms of glomerular organization and the number of glomeruli. According to the VFB term metadata, the adult antennal lobe has approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas the embryonic/larval antennal lobe has around 22 glomeruli. The VFB query counts also show that the adult stage has more returned part/glomerulus rows and broader neuron-class/data coverage for neurons with parts in the antennal lobe.

Both stages are glomerular, but the adult antennal lobe is represented as the more elaborated glomerular neuropil. The adult stage has more major connections/tracts, including the antennal nerve, antennal commissure, antennal lobe tracts, and broad root, whereas the larval stage has links to the antennal nerve input and the antero-basal tract.

In summary, the adult and larval antennal lobes are paired olfactory synaptic neuropils with glomerular organization, but they differ in terms of the number of glomeruli and the complexity of their organization. The adult antennal lobe has more glomeruli and more elaborate connections, whereas the larval antennal lobe has fewer glomeruli and simpler connections.

This information comes from the VFB term metadata and query counts, which provide evidence for the organization and structure of the antennal lobe in adult and larval Drosophila. VFB evidence supports answering directly and keeping counts scoped to the returned VFB terms/query rows.

status_messages.message: Building neuron profile for "giant fiber neuron"

results.response:
The giant fiber neuron (DNp01) is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle. The neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget.

VFB lists 22 available images of the giant fiber neuron, including images from the JRC2018U and JRCVNC2018U datasets. The neuron is connected to various downstream and upstream neurons, including the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum, and the gorget.

There are 14 transgene expression patterns available for the giant fiber neuron, including 5 GAL4 drivers and 5 split-GAL4/intersectional drivers. Some of the top tools include P{GMR78G07-GAL4}, P{GMR79D08-GAL4}, and P{GMR91H05-GAL4}.

One publication directly mentioning the giant fiber neuron is "The Drosophila connectome reveals axo-axonic synapses on descending neurons" (PMID: 42063566).
